reviews.text: It's the worst. I can't go into detail, but I don't recommend it.

This veterinarian is very caring and considerate of animals. They also take care to minimize the financial burden on pet owners.

However, perhaps because they are concerned about the financial burden, they don't perform many tests. It seems the hospital itself lacks the facilities for thorough examinations.

As a result, my beloved dog passed away after a night of agonizing screams and labored breathing.

They diagnosed pneumonia after one blood test and two X-rays, but after a week, then two weeks, there was no improvement. I rushed my dog ​​to the hospital every time he got sick, but they didn't perform any tests and simply gave him stronger antibiotics.

When I mentioned that my dog ​​had stopped eating, I was advised, "He absolutely has to eat. Filter wet food and feed it to him with a syringe," which I did.

However, because he wouldn't eat, he couldn't take his medication either. The morning after receiving a strong antibiotic intravenously that was supposed to last two weeks, he vomited. I rushed him to another hospital, where he was diagnosed with pancreatitis.

His gallbladder was filled with biliary sludge. Her digestive system was barely functioning, and her stomach was bloated from the food I was forcing her to eat as instructed. She wouldn't eat the meat and bananas she loved so much because she couldn't digest them anymore. I feel so terrible for forcing them into her mouth.

The blood tests at this hospital didn't show any signs of pancreatitis.

The antibiotics given for pneumonia ultimately backfired in treating her pancreatitis, and she passed away just three days later from DIC and sepsis, suffering so much that I wished her life would end quickly.

This happened several years ago, but this hospital specializes in dog teeth cleaning, and they said my dog's gums were "clean and fine," but she ended up having four teeth extracted under general anesthesia.

I wonder if I should have switched to a different hospital then.

So many regrets are flooding my mind, and I can't stop crying.

I think the doctor and staff are very kind. Thank you for the flowers.

Therefore, I think it's a good place to go for things that don't require a diagnosis, such as vaccinations.

However, if you notice even the slightest abnormality, I recommend that you cast aside any hesitation, such as "I've been indebted to them for so long," and go to a hospital that will perform proper examinations.

Illnesses cannot be diagnosed based on personality; they require scientific evidence from examinations.

Please click on the video to turn on the sound and listen to the screams. (The hospital said he wouldn't make it through the night, and after bringing him home, he screamed all night until he passed away.)
I'm posting this so that no other dog has to go through this experience.

I've been seeing him for my beloved dogs and cats for nearly 20 years. Due to various personal circumstances, I moved farther away, but I continued to go there. Last year, I switched to a nearby, trusted hospital where I could get a second opinion without an appointment and pay by credit card. If that hadn't happened, I would still be going there.

First of all, I think he has a strong personality and is very easy to misunderstand. He's generally unfriendly in person, and as the person below mentioned, he's even colder over the phone. It's true that he has a small staff, and unlike other hospitals, the treatment process is different in many ways, requiring the owner to hold the animal themselves. But he's very loving and kind to animals. There were times when I felt he lacked the ability to make decisive decisions. However, because making decisions on his own could cause problems, I think he deliberately leaves it up to the owner's judgment, or at least allows the owner to take responsibility for the animal. Owning an animal means taking full responsibility for it until the very end. Even with pets, owners need to be aware that they're entrusted with a precious life. He's kind to animals but very strict with their owners. However, he's kind to owners who treat them with love. I've been going there for nearly 20 years, and his words and attitude can be harsh at times, which can irritate me a few times, but I've gotten used to it. This is because he loves animals and I trust him to provide the best possible care for each animal at the time. If he can't do something for me, he'll introduce me to a highly rated veterinary hospital in Tamatsukuri that's even better, offers late-night emergency care, and is open late into the night. My beloved dog and cat have been saved so many times by the doctor. He's never motivated by money. Thanks to that, no matter how many times I begged him to accept card payments, he refused. I pleaded with him, saying that it would be a shame if the hospital didn't survive, and that it's convenient, cheap to begin with, and I don't mind charging more for appointments, so please accept card payments!!! But he said that with fees and other charges, the consultation fees would be even higher than they are now, so he wouldn't accept it. He said that as long as patients who trust him come, that's all that matters.

When I was crying at the hospital after my beloved dog of 17 years passed away, he cried with me.
They rescued a dying stray cat and spent three hours untangling its tangled fur, working tirelessly to treat it. When my mother's cat died of chronic renal failure, I called to tell them, crying and regretting that I should have paid more attention to it, and they encouraged me by saying, 'You did enough.'

I would recommend this hospital to anyone living in Kita Ward who lives nearby. It may be a bit intimidating for first-time patients, but I think the doctors have become much gentler than they were 20 years ago. I would also recommend this hospital to pet owners who consider animals to come first, rather than being friendly to their owners. On the flip side, the veterinary nurses at the reception desk are extremely polite, kind, and friendly.
Ten years ago, when I brought in a rescue cat, I was laughed at. It was like, "Have you ever owned a cat before? LOL." And the bill was about 20,000 yen. …

It's been over six months, but I finally feel ready to write this.

I've been going to this hospital for nearly ten years. …
